what: Written before untrusted.py is changed and before v2 is run on anything. Version 2 of the untrusted-text check, written ONLY from the misses of the 8 first advisories (results/advisory_replay_v1.json, the development set). Its result on the 31 held-out advisories (results/advisory_holdout_v1.json is v1's) is reported next to v1's, never instead of it.
changes: 1. Composite action files (action.yml, action.yaml, at any depth) are read as targets. Miss: embano1/wip, whose composite action.yml put an input into a shell line. Same line rules as for workflow files: only a command-like added line counts.

2. An expression is a hit when a stranger-text term is ANYWHERE inside the braces, not only first. Miss: gouef/githubtoplanguages, `${{ github.event.issue.title || github.event.pull_request.title }}`, which the first-position pattern did not match.
declined: 3. js-recon/js-recon: the vulnerable code passed event text through env: and used it as $BRANCH_NAME inside double quotes. That is GitHub's own recommended pattern and the shell does not run a quoted variable, so a rule for it would flag the fix. v2 does not flag env: assignments or $VARIABLE uses; that stays a deliberate limit. A rule for `${{ env.X }}` or `${{ steps.x.outputs.y }}` pasted into a shell line would come from the 31 held-out cases, so it would not be held out: it would be a separate v3, and its result on those 31 would be labelled as tuned.
unchanged: The list of stranger-text names, the GitLab variables, the interpreter and AI-tool lists, the single-quote rule, the command-like rule, the cap of 20. No constant is changed after any result is seen.
runs: A. development set: the 8 first advisories (expected to improve: the changes came from them; not held out).
B. held-out set: the 31 advisories of eval/advisory_holdout_rubric.json, run once.
C. false-alarm control: the same ordinary Mesa commits and the same agent-written commits as results/mesa_noise_v1.json and results/agent_noise_v1.json, untrusted check only.
D. the browser port web/try_checks.js must give identical answers (eval/try_agreement.py, a new registered version).

bars.C: speaks on at most 3% of the ordinary commits and 5% of the agent commits, as for v1; any commit where v2 speaks and v1 did not is read and listed

published: Advisory ids, repository names, commit ids, file paths, line numbers, kinds and counts. No diff text.
limits: The 31 were seen at the level of v1's result (which patterns it missed) before this file was written, and S1's report lists a pattern for every case. The two changes were chosen from the 8 and from the mechanism of the misses, not from reading the 31 diffs; this is stated so the reader can weigh it.
